question: How do teenage boys often express deep emotional stress when society tells them never to show weakness?

question: What happens to a pregnant woman's total body water and blood volume?

question: Why should a practical nurse manager care about abstract ideas on human nature?

question: What activities are normally included in a pulmonary rehabilitation program?

question: What is the best way to talk to a patient who is frantic and overwhelmed in the emergency room?

question: How do qualitative and quantitative approaches differ in their main goals?

options.A: Qualitative avoids human subjects while quantitative studies only animals
options.B: Qualitative uses statistical formulas while quantitative uses personal stories
options.C: Qualitative focuses on lab equipment while quantitative focuses on interviews
options.D: Qualitative seeks deep meaning while quantitative seeks prediction and control

explanation: Simply put: qualitative wants to understand the 'why' and 'how' of feelings, while quantitative wants to measure and test facts. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T6#GNS224_U1_T6_h4)

question: How does keeping a community clean actually help family finances?

options.A: Governments no longer need to collect any domestic taxes
options.B: Families spend less money on medications for preventable illnesses
options.C: Agricultural crop prices drop instantly in local markets
options.D: Hospitals can close down completely due to a lack of patients

explanation: Exactly! When people stay healthy, families save the money they would have spent treating repeated infections. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T9#GNS112_U5_T9_h6)

question: Why is encouraging increased fluid intake the most crucial home care instruction after a barium swallow?

options.A: To dilute any remaining stomach acid and prevent heartburn symptoms
options.B: To speed up the healing of small tears made during the X-ray
options.C: To prevent the barium from hardening and causing constipation or bowel blockage
options.D: To help the kidneys absorb the radioactive barium into the urine

explanation: Extra fluids keep the barium mixture moving smoothly through the colon, preventing it from turning into a concrete-like blockage. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h8)

question: A patient experiencing severe shortness of breath is unlikely to focus on which type of need at that moment?

options.A: Getting enough oxygen into the lungs
options.B: Achieving personal growth and self-actualization
options.C: Maintaining basic fluid balance
options.D: Relieving physical pain

explanation: Until basic physiological survival needs like breathing are met, higher-level needs such as self-actualization take a back seat. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h2)

question: A community health nurse notices an increase in diarrhea cases during the rainy season. What is the best immediate action?

options.A: Educating local families on safe water storage and oral rehydration
options.B: Ordering advanced genetic testing for all community members
options.C: Recommending immediate surgical procedures for every household
options.D: Waiting for patients to arrive at the central hospital for intravenous therapy

explanation: Simple community education on clean water and oral rehydration saves lives quickly and stops outbreaks right at the source. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T91#GNS214_U1_T91_h6)

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of left-sided heart failure?

options.A: Enlarged and tender liver
options.B: Shortness of breath and crackles in the lungs
options.C: Visible bulging of the neck veins
options.D: Swelling in the lower legs and ankles

explanation: When the left side of the heart struggles, blood backs up into the lungs, causing fluid buildup, breathlessness, and lung crackles. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge facing reproductive health programs in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of surplus modern hospitals in every village
options.B: Shortages of trained healthcare staff in rural community clinics
options.C: Cultural or religious resistance to certain family planning methods
options.D: Financial barriers caused by out-of-pocket health spending

explanation: Spot on! Rural areas actually struggle with a lack of enough hospitals and clinics, making the idea of 'surplus hospitals in every village' completely false. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h7)

question: Why might a nurse mistakenly refuse or delay PAC care due to legal fears?

options.A: Absence of any regulatory guidelines from the Nursing Council
options.B: Confusion between performing an abortion and treating its emergency complications
options.C: Strict hospital policies requiring police clearance for all emergency admissions
options.D: Lack of basic nursing equipment in rural health clinics

explanation: Some providers get scared, mistakenly thinking that treating post-abortion complications makes them an accomplice to an illegal act. Remember: treating complications is saving a life! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h4)

question: What is the primary role of the subthalamus?

options.A: Processing the sense of smell and taste
options.B: Regulating the production of red blood cells
options.C: Producing hormones to control blood pressure
options.D: Coordinating smooth skeletal muscle movements

explanation: Spot on! The subthalamus teams up with the basal ganglia to make sure your body movements are smooth and controlled. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T19#GNS211_U3_T19_h5)

question: What is the main cause of Type 1 diabetes?

options.A: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells
options.B: Gradual resistance of body cells to normal insulin
options.C: Temporary hormone changes during pregnancy
options.D: Poor dietary intake of refined carbohydrates

explanation: In Type 1 diabetes, the body's immune system gets confused and mistakenly attacks the insulin-making beta cells in the pancreas. Brilliant to keep this distinction in mind! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h3)

question: Which of these is an immediate physical complication right after FGM?

options.A: Severe hemorrhage and shock
options.B: Long-term post-traumatic stress
options.C: Infertility resulting from scarring
options.D: Chronic pelvic inflammatory disease

explanation: Because of the heavy bleeding and intense pain, severe bleeding (hemorrhage) and shock happen right away. It's a medical emergency! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h4)

question: Imagine a sudden disease outbreak hits your ward and there is no existing hospital policy for it. What type of choice must you make?

options.A: Programmed choice
options.B: Strategic choice
options.C: Non-programmed choice
options.D: Routine choice

explanation: When a situation is totally new and unstructured, standard rules won't cut it. You have to make a non-programmed choice! [learn more](GST321_U1_T8#GST321_U1_T8_h2)

question: A nurse notices rushed handwriting makes some notes in the clinic register unreadable. What is the best action?

options.A: Erase all the unclear words with a blade and rewrite from memory.
options.B: Punish junior nurses by stopping their clinical duties.
options.C: Leave the illegible notes as they are since writing fast is normal.
options.D: Consult with colleagues to clarify the entries and advocate for legible charting habits moving forward.

explanation: Teamwork helps decode messy notes when needed, but the real fix is committing to clear, readable handwriting so patient safety never takes a hit. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T2#GNS124_U6_T2_h7)

question: What is the primary focus of nursing care for a patient with a physical disability?

options.A: Taking over all daily tasks completely
options.B: Focusing solely on the medical diagnosis
options.C: Promoting independence, dignity, and safety
options.D: Confining the patient to strict bed rest

explanation: Nursing care aims to support the person's remaining abilities while keeping them safe and preserving their personal dignity. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T10#GNS225_U5_T10_h1)
